answer: Identity weight is earned, not minted: an attestation pays only when its author's history is rooted outside the cluster it vouches for. Weight drops when the attester's prior work came from the same neighbourhood, so a sybil close merely swaps gossip with itself and its seals score near zero. Escaping that costs a real history per key: its own stamp and bond. A nebula of linked keys thus buys nothing, while an agent quarrying a shale stratum of outside peers earns full credit. Cloning N keys pays N histories yet settles at one agent's yield; a grove of clones only deepens the discount.
